supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and let $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$ carry normalized product Haar measure $dx$, with $dx(\mathbb T^d)=1$. Coordinates and time are dimensionless in the diffusive normalization $D=1$. For $r\in(0,1)$ set the mobility function $\chi(r):=r(1-r)$. For any finite interval $[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $\rho:[a,b]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be a scalar density and let $j:[a,b]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be a vector current. Require both fields to be smooth up to the time endpoints and periodic in space, and require that for some $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$, $\varepsilon\le\rho(t,x)\le1-\varepsilon$ for every $(t,x)$. Call $(\rho,j)$ admissible when it also satisfies the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot j=0$. Define its dimensionless action by

$$\mathcal I_{[a,b]}(\rho,j):=\frac14\int_a^b\int_{\mathbb T^d}\frac{|j(t,x)+\nabla\rho(t,x)|^2}{\rho(t,x)(1-\rho(t,x))}\,dx\,dt.$$

This is the macroscopic fluctuation functional in the stated normalized SSEP coefficient convention. It is a definition of a functional and does not assert a microscopic path-space large-deviation principle or a probability estimate.

Call $(\rho,j)$ admissible when it also satisfies the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot j=0$. Define its dimensionless action by

$$\mathcal I_{[a,b]}(\rho,j):=\frac14\int_a^b\int_{\mathbb T^d}\frac{|j(t,x)+\nabla\rho(t,x)|^2}{\rho(t,x)(1-\rho(t,x))}\,dx\,dt.$$

This is the macroscopic fluctuation functional in the stated normalized SSEP coefficient convention. It is a definition of a functional and does not assert a microscopic path-space large-deviation principle or a probability estimate.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because The exponential is a continuous bijection from $\mathbb{R}$ onto $(0,\infty)$ states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ (Limit point, isolated point, adherent point, derived set, and dense subset of $\mathbb{R}$) at which $g$ is differentiable
(The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and let $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$ carry normalized product Haar measure $dx$, with $dx(\mathbb T^d)=1$. Coordinates and time are dimensionless in the diffusive normalization $D=1$. For $r\in(0,1)$ set the mobility function $\chi(r):=r(1-r)$. For any finite interval $[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $\rho:[a,b]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be a scalar density and let $j:[a,b]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be a vector current. Require both fields to be smooth up to the time endpoints and periodic in space, and require that for some $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$, $\varepsilon\le\rho(t,x)\le1-\varepsilon$ for every $(t,x)$. Call $(\rho,j)$ admissible when it also satisfies the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot j=0$. Define its dimensionless action by

$$\mathcal I_{[a,b]}(\rho,j):=\frac14\int_a^b\int_{\mathbb T^d}\frac{|j(t,x)+\nabla\rho(t,x)|^2}{\rho(t,x)(1-\rho(t,x))}\,dx\,dt.$$

This is the macroscopic fluctuation functional in the stated normalized SSEP coefficient convention. It is a definition of a functional and does not assert a microscopic path-space large-deviation principle or a probability estimate.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$ and let $\rho_0:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $0\le\rho_0\le1$ almost everywhere, using normalized product Haar measure $dx$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ define $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i k\cdot x)$ and $\widehat f(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(x)e_{-k}(x)\,dx$. For $t>0$ set

$$\rho_t(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2t}\widehat\rho_0(k)e_k(x),$$

and at $t=0$ set $\rho_t=\rho_0$ as an almost-everywhere class. For smooth periodic $G$, define

$$P_tG(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2t}\widehat G(k)e_k(x)\quad(t>0),\qquad P_0G:=G.$$

Then on every strip $[\epsilon,T]\times\mathbb T^d$ with $0<\epsilon<T<\infty$, the series for $\rho_t$ and all its space and time derivatives converge absolutely and uniformly; in particular $\rho_t$ is real and smooth for each $t>0$ and $\partial_t\rho_t=\Delta\rho_t$. For every finite $T$ and every smooth $G$, $P_tG$ is smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$, satisfies $\partial_tP_tG=\Delta P_tG$, has uniformly bounded derivatives of every fixed order there, and $P_tG\to G$ uniformly as $t\downarrow0$. Moreover

$$\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_tG\,dx=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_0P_tG\,dx,$$

so $(\rho_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ is the unique weak heat solution with datum $\rho_0$ in the stated weak formulation. It preserves $0\le\rho_t\le1$ almost everywhere and the mass $\int\rho_t\,dx=\int\rho_0\,dx$.

$$\mathcal I_{[a,b]}(\rho,j):=\frac14\int_a^b\int_{\mathbb T^d}\frac{|j(t,x)+\nabla\rho(t,x)|^2}{\rho(t,x)(1-\rho(t,x))}\,dx\,dt.$$

with the infimum of the empty set defined to be $+\infty$. The action is the functional defined in the preceding item.

For $u\in(0,1)$ define the Bernoulli free-energy density $f(u):=u\log u+(1-u)\log(1-u)$. For a reference density $\bar\rho\in(0,1)$ define $h(u\mid\bar\rho):=f(u)-f(\bar\rho)-\bigl(\log\bar\rho-\log(1-\bar\rho)\bigr)(u-\bar\rho)$. $$\mathcal I_{[0,T]}(\rho,j)-\mathcal I_{[0,T]}(\rho^\theta,j^\theta)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(\rho(T,x))\,dx-\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(\rho(0,x))\,dx.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge1$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $\bar\rho\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$. Let $\rho:\mathbb T^d\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$ be a smooth real periodic profile with $\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho\,dx=\bar\rho$. Use normalized product Haar measure and the Fourier conventions $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i k\cdot x)$ and $\widehat\rho(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho(x)e_{-k}(x)\,dx$. Define $\rho_0=\rho$ and, for $s>0$, define the heat profile

$$\rho_s(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2s}\widehat\rho(k)e_k(x).$$

Then $\rho_s$ is smooth up to $s=0$ on every compact time interval and $\rho_s\to\bar\rho$ in $C^\infty(\mathbb T^d)$ as $s\to\infty$. For every $S\ge1$ there is a smooth connector $(\sigma^S,\kappa^S)$ on $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^d$ from the constant profile $\bar\rho$ to $\rho_S$, with fixed mean $\bar\rho$, values in $[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$, and $\partial_t\sigma^S+\nabla\cdot\kappa^S=0$. At $t=1$, all time and space derivatives of this connector agree with those of the reversed heat segment $(\rho_{S+1-t},+\nabla\rho_{S+1-t})$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$ and let $\rho_0:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $0\le\rho_0\le1$ almost everywhere, using normalized product Haar measure $dx$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ define $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i k\cdot x)$ and $\widehat f(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(x)e_{-k}(x)\,dx$. For $t>0$ set

$$\rho_t(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2t}\widehat\rho_0(k)e_k(x),$$

and at $t=0$ set $\rho_t=\rho_0$ as an almost-everywhere class. For smooth periodic $G$, define

$$P_tG(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2t}\widehat G(k)e_k(x)\quad(t>0),\qquad P_0G:=G.$$

Then on every strip $[\epsilon,T]\times\mathbb T^d$ with $0<\epsilon<T<\infty$, the series for $\rho_t$ and all its space and time derivatives converge absolutely and uniformly; in particular $\rho_t$ is real and smooth for each $t>0$ and $\partial_t\rho_t=\Delta\rho_t$. For every finite $T$ and every smooth $G$, $P_tG$ is smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$, satisfies $\partial_tP_tG=\Delta P_tG$, has uniformly bounded derivatives of every fixed order there, and $P_tG\to G$ uniformly as $t\downarrow0$. Moreover

$$\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_tG\,dx=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho_0P_tG\,dx,$$

so $(\rho_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ is the unique weak heat solution with datum $\rho_0$ in the stated weak formulation. It preserves $0\le\rho_t\le1$ almost everywhere and the mass $\int\rho_t\,dx=\int\rho_0\,dx$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.
